h1: The 7 Best Standing Desk Converters for Two Monitors, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Dual Monitor Converters: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 dual monitor standing desk converters compared on platform width, built-in mounts, lift type and budget, from VIVO to Vari.
summary: The Vari VariDesk Pro Plus 48 is the one to buy if you want two monitors on a wide, proven platform, and the Pro Plus 36 gets you the same lift in a smaller footprint. The VERSADESK PowerPro is the best electric option, the Mount-It is the pick if you want arms included, and the VIVO 32 is the budget route to two screens.
intro: The usual mistake with a dual monitor converter is measuring the monitors and forgetting the desk. Two screens plus their stands can need more width than the converter platform offers, and a platform that overhangs the desk leaves you with no room for anything else. Width is the first filter, long before lift mechanics or colour.

This ranking sorts seven converters by how well they carry two displays. We reviewed the listings and published specs, comparing platform width, whether monitor mounts are built in, how the lift works, and which price bracket each sits in. Where a listing gives no weight capacity or travel figure, we say so and do not invent one.

products.name: Vari VariDesk Pro Plus 48
products.verdict: The 48 inch platform that gives two monitor bases room to breathe.
products.description:
The Pro Plus 48 is a 48 inch wide sit-stand converter with 11 height settings, sold in the $500+ bracket. Its width is the headline: two monitor stands fit side by side with space left for a keyboard and notes.

It is first because width is what a dual setup needs most. A narrower platform forces monitors to crowd the centre or hang off the edge, and the Pro Plus 48 avoids both problems. The 11 height settings let you fine tune where the screens sit relative to your eyes. The cost is the price, the highest here, and the sheer footprint, which only suits a desk wide enough to take a 48 inch unit.

Buy it if you have a large desk, use two full-size screens and want a converter that has a long track record. Skip it if your desk is under about five feet wide or the budget is tight.
pros: Room left for keyboard and papers
cons: Needs a wide desk to fit
products.idealFor: People with large desks who run two full-size monitors.
products.skipIf: Your desk is narrow or the budget is limited.

products.name: Vari VariDesk Pro Plus 36
products.verdict: Vari's dual-monitor capable 36 inch model at a lower price than the 48.
products.description:
The Pro Plus 36 shares the 11 height settings of its larger sibling on a 36 inch platform, in the $200 to $500 bracket. It is the practical way into the Vari line for a standard desk.

It ranks second because it keeps the proven mechanism while costing less and fitting more desks. The tradeoff is directly related to width: two big monitors on 36 inches will sit tight, and it is easier with smaller screens or two compact bases. Choose the 48 if your displays are wide, and this one if desk space is the limit.

It suits most home offices with a desk about four to five feet wide. Skip it if you run two ultrawide or oversized panels.
pros: Lower price than the wide model
cons: Still costs more than budget rivals
products.idealFor: Home offices that need a proven dual-monitor converter.
products.skipIf: You use two oversized or ultrawide screens.

products.name: VERSADESK PowerPro 36 Inch Electric Standing Desk Converter
products.verdict: A 36 inch platform with push-button electric lift for heavier monitor loads.
products.description:
The PowerPro is a 36 inch converter with electric push-button lift, in the $200 to $500 bracket. The motor is the whole story, because two monitors and their stands can be heavy enough to make a manual spring lift awkward.

It ranks third because effortless adjustment changes how often you actually stand. A manual unit loaded with two screens needs a deliberate heave, and many owners stop raising it. The electric model removes that friction. It sits behind the Varis because it needs a power outlet near the desk and adds a motor that can eventually fail, and the listing gives no capacity or speed figures to compare.

Pick it if your setup is heavy or you want one-touch changes through the day. Skip it if you want a mechanism with nothing to plug in.
cons: No capacity figure on the listing
products.idealFor: Heavy dual-monitor setups where manual lifting is a chore.
products.skipIf: You want a purely mechanical unit with no cable.

products.name: Mount-It! Standing Desk Converter Dual Monitor
products.verdict: Two screen mounts included, so the platform holds the desk and the arms hold the displays.
products.description:
The Mount-It converter ships with integrated dual monitor mounts, in the $200 to $500 bracket. That moves the screens off the platform and onto arms, which frees surface for the keyboard and mouse.

It ranks fourth because the built-in mounts solve a real problem: monitor stands eat the work surface, and two of them eat a lot. The tradeoff is that monitors must be VESA compatible to use arms, so older panels without mounting holes need an adapter. You also lose the freedom to place each screen anywhere on an open deck.

It is a good buy for VESA-ready monitors and for people who want a tidy desk. Skip it if your screens lack mounting holes.
cons: Less freedom than an open platform
products.idealFor: Buyers with VESA monitors who want a clean desk.
products.skipIf: Your monitors cannot accept an arm.

products.name: VIVO 32 Inch Standing Desk Converter with Dual Monitor Stand
products.verdict: A 32 inch platform with an integrated stand for two 13 to 30 inch monitors, cheaply.
products.description:
The VIVO 32 inch converter integrates a dual stand for 13 to 30 inch monitors, in the $100 to $200 bracket. It is the least expensive route in this list to having both screens and the lift in a single box.

It ranks fifth because the 32 inch width and the screen size window set clear limits. Two 27 inch monitors are within range but will fill the platform, and anything larger falls outside the stated 30 inch maximum. It does what it promises for the price, but the smaller footprint leaves less desk room than the wider models.

Choose it for a small desk, two modest monitors and a firm budget. Skip it if you run screens bigger than 30 inches.
pros: Dual stand integrated into the unit
Low price for a dual setup
cons: Screens above 30 inches do not fit
products.idealFor: Small desks and budget-minded dual-screen users.
products.skipIf: Your monitors are larger than 30 inches.

products.name: VIVO Black 42 Inch Standing Desk Converter DESK-V000VL
products.verdict: A 42 inch open platform that lets you place any two monitor stands where you like.
products.description:
The DESK-V000VL is a 42 inch open platform with no built-in monitor stand, in the $200 to $500 bracket. You bring your own stands or arms and arrange them freely.

It lands sixth because open space is a double-edged feature. You can mix a 27 inch and a 24 inch screen, or add a laptop riser, without fighting a fixed bracket. But the listing offers little beyond width, so it ranks below units that include mounts or a motor at similar money.

It suits people who already own good monitor stands and want a wide base. Skip it if you want everything included.
products.idealFor: Owners of existing stands who want a wide base.
products.skipIf: You need mounts included in the box.

products.name: FITUEYES Height Adjustable Standing Desk 36 Inch Wide Converter
products.verdict: A 36 inch open platform in the $100 to $200 bracket for your own monitor stands.
products.description:
The FITUEYES converter is a 36 inch open sit-stand platform in the $100 to $200 bracket. It offers the width of a mid-range unit without the cost.

It ranks last because open 36 inch decks are tight for two bases, and the listing offers few specifics on capacity or lift mechanism. For two compact monitors on slim stands it works, but you will feel the edges sooner than on the 42 or 48 inch options.

It is a sensible choice for a budget buyer with small monitors. Skip it if you run two large screens.
pros: Low price for a 36 inch deck
products.idealFor: Budget buyers running two smaller monitors.
products.skipIf: Your monitors are large or very heavy.

whatMatters.detail: Width decides whether two monitors sit comfortably or crowd each other. Two 27 inch screens plus stands generally want more than 36 inches of clear surface. Measure your monitors with their stands, add room for a keyboard, and compare against the listed platform width and your desk.

Some converters have an open deck for your own stands, and others integrate arms or a dual stand. Built-in mounts save surface space but need VESA compatible monitors and respect stated size ranges. Check your monitors for mounting holes on the back before choosing.

Manual lifts are simple and need no outlet, while electric lifts remove effort when two screens add weight. The easier the lift, the more often people use it. Look for push-button wording on the listing and note whether a power outlet is required.

The number of stopping points affects how closely you can match your eye line. The Vari models list 11 settings, which is a useful fine-tuning range. Check the minimum and maximum heights against your own seated and standing elbow heights.

A converter must fit the desk beneath it with room to spare for cables and the base. Overhang can make the unit unstable or block drawers. Compare the platform depth and width with your desk, and leave a margin.

howToChoose.intro: Width is the first filter for a two-monitor converter, so match it to your desk and your screens.

cards.label: Open platform
cards.text: You use any monitor stands and place them freely. The VIVO 42 and FITUEYES 36 are the open-deck picks, and they accept screens of mixed sizes.

cards.label: Built-in mounts
cards.text: Arms or an integrated stand hold the screens, leaving more room for peripherals. The Mount-It and the VIVO 32 follow this model but require compatible monitors.

howToChoose.note: Open platforms are the safer default if your monitors vary, and mounts are better when screens are VESA ready.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: At least 42 inches of platform, or arms that lift the screens off the deck. Anything narrower will feel cramped once stands and a keyboard are in place.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Vari VariDesk Pro Plus 48 and VIVO 42 offer the width, and the Mount-It takes the screens off the surface. The VIVO 32 handles 27 inch screens only snugly.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You stand for long stretches, use heavy screens or want fewer compromises on width. The Vari 48 and the electric VERSADESK are the upgrades worth considering.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Your monitors are small and your desk is compact. The VIVO 32 and FITUEYES 36 cover the basics at a modest price.

faq.q: Will a converter fit my existing desk?
faq.a: Measure the desk depth and width, then compare with the platform size on the listing. Leave a margin so the base does not overhang the edge. A 48 inch unit needs a desk at least that wide to sit properly.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake with dual monitor converters?
faq.a: Buying on lift features and ignoring width. Two monitors plus stands need space, and a narrow platform leaves them cramped. Measure the setup you plan to use before buying.

faq.q: Is an electric converter worth it over a manual one?
faq.a: It is when two heavy monitors make a manual lift tiring. The VERSADESK removes effort, which tends to increase how often you stand. If your screens are light, a manual Vari model saves money and avoids a power cord.

faq.q: How do I set up monitor arms on a converter?
faq.a: Check that your monitors have VESA mounting holes on the rear, then attach the arms to the platform following the instructions. Route cables before raising the unit to avoid tugging on ports. Test the full height range with the screens attached.
Very little. Occasionally check that fasteners are tight and wipe the surface. On the electric model, keep the cable clear of the lifting mechanism and avoid overloading it.

faq.q: Can I use ultrawide monitors on these?
faq.a: Only with care. The VIVO 32 lists support for screens up to 30 inches, and ultrawide panels are wide and heavy. Choose a wider open platform like the Vari 48 and check your monitor weight and stand width first.

finalTake: Buy the Vari VariDesk Pro Plus 48 if you have the desk and want the best two-screen platform. The Pro Plus 36 is the smarter pick for a standard desk, and the VERSADESK PowerPro is the one to get if lifting is a chore. The Mount-It suits VESA monitors, while the VIVO 32 is the budget answer for small screens. Measure your monitors first.
